result.reason: Section 20(d) reaches the preferred position: Sparkling may assign without consent to affiliates and M&A successors; Garman's consent right is subject to a reasonableness standard; Garman may never assign to a Sparkling competitor; and Sparkling's change of control creates no Garman termination right. However, the Section 3(c) amendment is overbroad because “or as permitted under Section 20(d)” grammatically applies not only to assignment but also to transferring, leasing, exporting, or sublicensing the Work. That may unintentionally expand Sparkling's rights concerning the Work and does not preserve unrelated commercial intent. The cleaner edit would delete only the assignment restriction from Section 3(c), or expressly clarify that Section 20(d) applies solely to assignment of the Agreement. Allowing assignment “in whole or in part” also goes beyond what the preferred position expressly requires.
